quota-reservation-under-concurrency-01.graded_text: Starting an upload atomically reserves its declared size against remaining capacity, counting other open reservations, so parallel uploads cannot together pass the cap. A check of used plus size alone is identified as insufficient.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:9 says the old check is not enough: "Each check sees the same `used`, so all 8 pass and together can go well over 10 GB." Lines 32-38: "**startUpload**, inside one transaction: ... Reject with `quota_exceeded` if `used + open reservations + size > cap` ... The upload row is the reservation." Line 79 requires a serializable transaction or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. The code matches at packages/backend/src/uploads.ts:58-74: `ctx.db.transaction(...)`, `liveReservedBytes(tx, ...)`, `if (account.used + reserved.bytes + input.size > account.cap) throw new QuotaExceeded`, then `tx.uploads.insert({... status: "pending", expiresAt ...})`.

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-02.graded_text: Finalize commits usage from the verified stored size and turns the reservation into usage, and a failed, abandoned, or expired upload releases its reservation through a stated cleanup path.

votes.e: Commit: docs/quota-accounting.md:49 says "Otherwise do `used += measured size`, mark it `ready` with `storedSize`", and line 51 says "Charging happens once per upload, from the measured size, in the same transaction that closes the reservation." The code at uploads.ts:133-134 is `used: account.used + stored.size` and `status: "ready", storedSize: stored.size`. Release: doc line 42 says "Open reservations are worked out from the upload rows at read time ... an abandoned reservation stops counting once it expires, with no sweeper and no counter drift." Failed rows drop out because only `listPendingByAccount` rows within `expiresAt > now` count (uploads.ts:45-46), and size_mismatch, abandoned and quota_exceeded uploads are patched to `status: "failed"` (uploads.ts:105, 111, 127).

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-03.graded_text: A retried finalize counts the upload's size once, not twice, in both the design and the changed code.

votes.e: Design, docs/quota-accounting.md:47: "Already `ready` → return success and charge nothing." Line 49: "re-read the upload (a concurrent finalize may have won)". Code, uploads.ts:96-98: `if (upload.status === "ready") { await enqueueSummary(ctx, upload); return ... }`. Inside the transaction at uploads.ts:117-118: `const current = await tx.uploads.get(upload.id); if (current.status === "ready") return "ready";`. The summary job is deduplicated by `{ key: upload.summaryAttemptId }` (uploads.ts:172).

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-04.graded_text: The user's storage quota is kept separate from the model provider's cost: the design says a failed summary can still cost the product money and records or bounds that cost, rather than promising failed work is free.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:16-19 sets up "Two ledgers": "Storage allowance (user-facing...)" and "Summary spend (internal...) Counts what the model provider charges us". Line 60: "The summarize job calls `settleSummaryAttempt` with the real provider cost **whether it succeeded or failed**. A failed attempt costs the user's allowance nothing, but its cost is still counted against our spend." The code records it at uploads.ts:202: `status: input.outcome, costMicros: input.costMicros`, and it is bounded by `SUMMARY_SPEND_LIMIT_MICROS` (uploads.ts:155).

quota-reservation-under-concurrency-05.graded_text: Finalize compares the actual stored size with the reserved size and refuses or corrects a mismatch, so a client cannot reserve a small size and store a large object.

votes.e: docs/quota-accounting.md:48: "If the measured size is larger than declared (or larger than the per-item limit), fail it as `size_mismatch` and delete the object." Line 40 binds the PUT: "only accepts `Content-Length = size`". Code at uploads.ts:110-113: `if (stored.size > upload.size || stored.size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES) { ... status: "failed", failureKind: "size_mismatch" ... ctx.storage.delete(upload.id) ...}`. A smaller object is charged at its measured size (uploads.ts:133), so under-declaring never pays off.

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] The hidden summary spend ceiling quietly overrides the brief's decision that "Every uploaded document gets an AI summary" (docs/brief.md), on every plan. docs/quota-accounting.md:91 sets "Internal spend limit $2.00 per account per UTC month, estimate $0.02 per summary ... They allow roughly 100 summaries a month on any plan." Line 75 adds "(Never mention the spend limit or its number.)" A free user who uploads their 101st document in a month gets a `paused` summary with no explanation, and so does a paying user. The brief gives no evidence that every-document summaries are unsafe at that volume. The ships-as-code constant is `SUMMARY_SPEND_LIMIT_MICROS = 2_000_000` (uploads.ts:20). (held)
